theme: Dead to sin, alive to God; slaves of righteousness
readingInstruction: Read Romans 6:1-23. You studied the first half of this chapter in the doctrinal pause on union with Christ. Today read the whole chapter, and focus on the language of slavery and freedom in verses 15-23.
settingTheScene: Paul has said that believers have died to sin. In the second half of chapter 6, he uses the picture of slavery to explain the change of masters. Everyone serves something. The question is not whether we will be slaves but whose. Paul’s readers in Rome knew slavery well, and the image was both vivid and humbling.
observation: “What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound?” (6:1).
“By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?” (6:2).
“For one who has died has been set free from sin” (6:7).
“Present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life” (6:13).
“But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed” (6:17).
“And, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness” (6:18).
“But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life” (6:22).
“For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord” (6:23).
interpretation:
The chapter opens with an objection that Paul takes very seriously. If grace is free, why not sin more? The answer in the first half is union with Christ. In the second half, Paul adds a second argument: the idea of two masters.

In verses 12 to 14, he gives practical commands. “Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, to make you obey its passions.” Sin is a king. It still tries to rule. Do not present your members, hands, eyes, tongue, to sin as instruments of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life. And the promise: “Sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace.” Grace is not a license, but a power.

Then the second question: “Are we to sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means!” Paul turns to slavery. “Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness?” There is no neutral ground. We are slaves of sin or slaves of righteousness. But the change has happened: “Thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed.” The gospel has teaching, and obedience from the heart is the evidence of conversion.

The paradox is that serving God is freedom. Slavery to sin offers apparent liberty but delivers shame: “What fruit were you getting at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.” Slavery to God yields fruit that leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life. The believer’s obedience is not a way to earn salvation, but a growing holiness that expresses it.

The chapter ends with one of the best-known verses of Romans: “For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Wages are earned; a gift is not. Sin pays what it owes: death. God gives what we have not earned: eternal life. And it is found only “in Christ Jesus our Lord.” The verse sums up the whole letter so far.
connection: John 8:34-36 says everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin, but the Son sets free. Galatians 5:1 says for freedom Christ has set us free. 1 Peter 2:16 calls us to live as people who are free, yet servants of God. Matthew 6:24 says no one can serve two masters. Ephesians 2:1-3 describes our former life. 2 Timothy 2:19 speaks of departing from iniquity. Titus 2:11-14 speaks of grace training us to renounce ungodliness. Genesis 2:17 and Ezekiel 18:20 speak of death as the wage of sin.
application:
Ask what has been mastering you. Name the idol, habit, or fear that most often rules your decisions.

Present yourself to God today. Give him your hands, your eyes, and your tongue for one task.

Memorize Romans 6:23 and share it with a friend.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for setting you free from sin.
Offer yourself to him as an instrument of righteousness, and name one way.
Ask him not to let sin reign in you.
